q: What should I read from a coal invoice to calculate emissions?
title: Coal invoice: what to read
short: The quantity received in tonnes, the grade or GCV, and the moisture basis. Emissions need tonnes burnt and energy content: tonnes × GCV converted to NCV × the IPCC factor for the coal type. If the invoice gives only a grade, use your own lab GCV.
audience: Boiler and kiln operators buying Indian or imported coal

ul: Tonnes dispatched and received, and any shortage.
Grade, GCV and the basis, such as air dried, as received or GAR.
Total moisture and ash, if stated.
Tonnes actually burnt, from stock changes.
The basis used for the factor, kept consistent.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel invoices into a dated, fingerprinted record, so each figure shows the quantity, factor and document it came from.
